title: Arachnid Core custody record
description:
One line of <container>/custody.log. Each line is `<signature-hex> <record-json>`, where the signature is Ed25519 over the exact bytes following the first space. This schema describes the record JSON only.

The log is a hash chain: `prev` holds the SHA-256 of the entire previous line, so removing or reordering a record breaks verification. Records are never re-serialized during verification, so byte-level canonicalization is not required of consumers -- but a consumer that rewrites a record cannot re-sign it without the operator's key.

seq.description: Zero-based position in the log. Must increase by exactly one per line.

ts_utc.description: Wall clock at the moment of the event, RFC 3339 UTC. Subject to clock adjustment on the examined host; use mono_ns for relative ordering.

mono_ns.description: Nanoseconds since container creation, from a monotonic clock. Unaffected by NTP steps or a hostile host changing its wall clock mid-collection.

operator.description: Operator identity as supplied at collection. Self-asserted; attributable only through the signing key.

event.description: run_start carries the manifest digest; artifact records one collected file; note records something that produced no artifact; run_end closes the log.

name.description: Artifact path relative to <container>/artifacts/. Required when event is "artifact".

sha256.description: Digest of the artifact, computed at the moment of collection. Absent on a dry run, where nothing was written.

size.description: Artifact size in bytes at collection time.

detail.description: Free text for note records: the invocation, a degraded collector, an external tool that was run.

prev.description: SHA-256 of the previous log line's exact bytes, signature included. Sixty-four zeroes for seq 0.
